report:
**Conclusion**
Yes, denosumab (Prolia) significantly reduces the risk of vertebral fractures in individuals with osteoporosis.

**Key Evidence**
* **Vertebral Risk Reduction:** In the landmark Phase III FREEDOM trial, postmenopausal women with osteoporosis receiving denosumab (60 mg subcutaneously every 6 months) had a **68% relative risk reduction** in new vertebral fractures over 3 years compared to placebo.
* **Other Fracture Sites:** The trial also showed reductions in hip fractures (by 40%) and nonvertebral fractures (by 20%).
* **Long-Term & Real-World Efficacy:** Extension and real-world studies spanning up to 10 years demonstrate sustained increases in bone mineral density and persistently low rates of vertebral fractures in both postmenopausal women and men with osteoporosis.
* **Discontinuation Warning:** Stopping denosumab abruptly without transitioning to another bone-protective medication (such as a bisphosphonate) can trigger rapid bone loss and a rebound risk of multiple vertebral fractures.

**Sources**
1. *New England Journal of Medicine*: https://www.nejm.org/doi/full/10.1056/nejmoa0809493
2. *American Academy of Family Physicians*: https://www.aafp.org/afp/2019/0501/od1
3. *PMC (10-Year FREEDOM Extension Review)*: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8799550/
4. *Osteoporosis International*: https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s00198-024-07381-1
